Operational walkthroughs and interpretation
Dine-in example — analyst walkthrough
A guest is seated, a captain selects the table and items, preparation tickets reach the correct kitchen stations,
further items remain attached to the visit, food is marked ready, and the cashier presents the bill. The guest
pays using one or more tenders. Only the supported finalisation workflow should release the table, create the
correct payment record and leave the audit trail. Test a correction at each stage; a successful simple sale does
not validate the exceptional paths.
Daily receipt example — illustrative, not Petpooja output
Suppose today’s new sales are ₹10,000: ₹4,000 cash, ₹3,000 UPI and ₹3,000 sold on credit. An older customer
also clears ₹1,000 in cash today. Today’s customer collections are ₹8,000, while today’s sales remain ₹10,000.
Cash collected is ₹5,000 before expenses, withdrawals, refunds or opening float. New credit adds ₹3,000 to
receivables and the old collection reduces them by ₹1,000. Ask the software to demonstrate all four figures
without counting the old collection as new sales.

Ingredient-control example — illustrative
A recipe uses 18 g of coffee per drink. Selling 100 drinks implies 1.8 kg theoretical consumption. Actual stock
loss could be higher because of calibration, spillage or unrecorded drinks. Inventory automation is useful only if
purchases, recipe units, wastage and physical counts are recorded consistently. A cost report must state
whether it uses theoretical consumption, actual counts or another configured basis.
Aggregator example — analyst walkthrough
An order can be successfully delivered while the payout contains deductions or a different final status. Check the
external order identifier, gross value, discounts, tax, commission, fees and paid amount separately.
Reconciliation should create an explainable exception list; it does not by itself demonstrate that the aggregator
has accepted a claim or paid a recovery.
Permissions example — analyst walkthrough
Give a cashier only the access required for a shift, then attempt a discount beyond policy, a payment correction,
a cancellation and a cross-outlet export. Repeat with a supervisor. Review the log afterwards. A screen being
hidden is only one part of effective permission enforcement; the vendor should also demonstrate the operation
cannot be completed through another app or export route.

Public documentation is useful but contains inconsistencies. The following issues materially affect how the

Finding
Evidence and implication
Different feature counts
Official pages use 80+, 94+ and 100+ report language, and varying integration counts [S05,

Build versus tier
The four-build comparison and the plan page describe different dimensions [S02, S29]. An

Local migration wording
One guide describes Local as a fresh setup; another describes moving between types as a

scope.
AI inventory descriptions
The feature roundup describes automatic stock updating, while the dedicated AI guide
describes an insights tool [S30, S31]. Ask for the exact product screen and write capabilities.

The batch guide contains conflicting wording about spreadsheet updates to average purchase
price and overlapping date-limit descriptions [S54]. Confirm rules against the deployed
version.

The menu-quantity article records limitations around editing bills, add-ons, resets and printer
configuration [S50]. These should be reproduced or confirmed fixed during a demo.

The barcode article’s input weight and worked calculation do not align [S45]. Use
independently calculated test weights instead of copying that example.

In v125, an out-of-stock QR heading repeats announcement-banner wording [S35]. That

confused with merchant-accessible settings.

names
The public pricing page does not provide a clean, reliably extracted numeric quote or
complete entitlement matrix; older release notes use other bundle names [S29, S38]. Request

Security and export gaps
This review did not establish account-wide MFA, log immutability, backup recovery
commitments, API quotas, full data-export formats or deletion timelines. These remain open
vendor questions.
No hands-on validation
Usability, latency, crash recovery, offline conflict handling, payment callbacks and printer
behavior were not tested. Public performance and savings claims are not independent
benchmarks.
Other details requiring direct verification include full discount-stacking rules, seat/course handling, kitchen re-fire
behavior, refund approval and gateway scope, credit ageing and reminders, stock-reservation timing, transfer
shortage approvals, recipe history, API/webhook documentation, historical imports, retention and audit-log
export. The absence of public evidence does not prove the feature is absent.
Forty demonstration and acceptance scenarios
These are proposed checks, not completed tests or claims about guaranteed outcomes. Run them in a
vendor-provided test account with synthetic data. Ask the presenter to demonstrate the actual installed build
and retain screenshots, exports and version details for any critical requirement.

Commercial and implementation questions
No reliable fixed subscription total is quoted here. Pricing, build coverage, hardware, partner services and
add-ons need a dated, itemised proposal. The current public plan page should be treated as a starting point.
[S29]
1. Exact product/build/version and number of outlets, terminals, users and devices covered.
2. Core/Growth/Scale entitlement line items; each paid marketplace service and renewal cost.
3. Installation, training, menu/recipe loading, data migration and any onsite visit costs.
4. Kitchen/captain/QR/kiosk/token/reservation devices, software licences and warranties.
5. Payment hardware rental, gateway charges, settlement arrangements and refund charges.
6. SMS/WhatsApp credits, sender onboarding, loyalty/gift-card charges and message limits.
7. Aggregator, ERP/accounting and custom API setup, maintenance, quotas and support ownership.
8. Backups, recovery commitments, retention, bulk export, account closure and data handover.
9. Support response targets, escalation contacts, language coverage and replacement timelines.
10. Any tax, annual increase, cancellation condition, trial limit or geography/build exclusion.
Suggested rollout sequence
First validate the menu, taxes, printers, tenders, user access and closing reports. Next establish purchase
entries, recipe units, opening stock, wastage and physical counts. Then enable online integrations and complete
payout reconciliation. Add guest-facing ordering, loyalty and operational apps after the underlying records
reconcile. Finish with multi-outlet standardisation, integrations and AI-assisted analysis. This is the analyst’s
implementation recommendation, not a required Petpooja installation sequence.
Assessment to use when reviewing Petpooja
The documented strength is breadth across restaurant transactions, stock, guest service and multi-outlet
control. The practical question is whether the chosen build performs the complete workflows your outlet needs,
including corrections and recovery. Prioritise a coherent demonstration of ordering, money and stock over the
number of advertised features. Treat unresolved version, entitlement and documentation issues as conditions to
clarify before relying on them operationally.

What still cannot be called complete
A public review cannot certify that every button, dropdown choice, validation rule and backend setting has been
captured. Neither report should be described as a complete screen-by-screen operating manual. Some screens
appear only with particular permissions, data, paid services or regional integrations.
A final installation-specific audit needs a current screen/menu inventory, subscription and module list,
role-permission export, device/app version list, representative configuration screens and sample reports. The
highest-value remaining areas are refund and reversal behavior, API/webhook contracts, data export and
retention, backup restoration, failed-sync recovery, report definitions and partner-specific limitations. These are
verification gaps, not claims that Petpooja lacks those capabilities.
For a detailed screen-by-screen operating manual, each workflow should record its starting state, exact
navigation, visible fields, allowed inputs, default values, validations, permitted roles, save/cancel behavior,
resulting records and recovery steps. That requires direct observation of the selected build. The current
supplement adds the publicly supported details without inventing unseen screens.
